fleetMemoryScratch.text: A dispatch's 'N rail keys x M counties = X pairs' framing can silently conflate the GATE's per-rail-key evaluation with the SLATE's per-representative-key addressing when a rail group (here, the 4-key setback family) was designed with one gate covering several sibling values. Before adding a slate entry, grep resolveAllowlist's actual call sites for the literal rail-key string, not just the rail's presence in rail-keys.js or parcel_gate_verdict -- the gate can legitimately evaluate a key that no slate entry could ever address.

When a dispatch's headline pair-count does not match what a grep of the real call sites supports, the correct move (per DEV_PROCESS 3.2/1.4) is to do the smaller, correct edit and document the reconciliation in the code's own comment plus every checkpoint -- not to pad the Set to hit the stated number, and not to silently do less without flagging it.

gcloud run services/revisions describe needs the SERVICE's own GCP project, which can differ from the project holding an unrelated Neon-adjacent resource this program also uses (hauska-prod-497015 for the Factory host vs legacy-design-tools-prod for cortex-api's Cloud Run service) -- `gcloud projects list` plus a quick describe-probe across the candidates found it in under a minute; worth checking early rather than assuming the project used for a DB secret is also the deploy target's project.
